title: Opening Night: General Knowledge
description: Four rounds of crowd-pleasing general knowledge that ramp from warm-ups to cheer-worthy closers, capped by a final wager.

questions.prompt: Guacamole is made primarily from which fruit?
questions.answer_note: source: Encyclopaedia Britannica — guacamole is a mashed-avocado dip; the name comes from Nahuatl 'ahuacamolli', avocado sauce.

questions.prompt: In The Wizard of Oz, what is the name of Dorothy's dog?
questions.answer_note: source: The Wizard of Oz (MGM, 1939) — Dorothy's Cairn Terrier is named Toto.

questions.prompt: The Beatles formed in which English city?
questions.answer_note: source: The Beatles Story museum, Liverpool — the band formed in Liverpool in 1960.

questions.prompt: Which element has the chemical symbol Au?
questions.answer_note: source: IUPAC periodic table — gold's symbol Au comes from the Latin 'aurum'; silver is Ag, aluminum Al, argon Ar.

questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Australia?
questions.answer_note: source: Australian government — purpose-built Canberra became the capital as a 1913 compromise between rivals Sydney and Melbourne.

questions.prompt: What is the term for a word or phrase that reads the same forwards and backwards?
questions.answer_note: source: Merriam-Webster — a palindrome reads the same backward as forward, e.g. 'racecar' or 'madam'.

questions.prompt: The Great Wall of China is visible to the naked eye from the Moon.
questions.answer_note: source: NASA — Apollo astronauts confirmed no human-made structures, the Great Wall included, are visible unaided from the Moon.

questions.prompt: How many wives did King Henry VIII of England have?
questions.answer_note: source: Historic Royal Palaces — Henry VIII married 6 times between 1509 and 1543, from Catherine of Aragon to Catherine Parr.

questions.prompt: Tequila must be made from which plant?
questions.answer_note: source: Mexican official standard (NOM) — tequila must be distilled from Weber blue agave, which is not a cactus.

questions.prompt: Which is the only letter of the alphabet that appears in no US state name?
questions.answer_note: source: the 50 US state names — every other letter appears somewhere: J in New Jersey, X in Texas, Z in Arizona; Q appears nowhere.

questions.prompt: In the sitcom Friends, what is the name of the coffee shop where the gang hangs out?
questions.answer_note: source: Friends (NBC, 1994-2004) — Central Perk is the group's Manhattan coffee house; Café Nervosa is from Frasier.

questions.prompt: What color jersey does the overall leader of the Tour de France wear?
questions.answer_note: source: Tour de France — the general-classification leader has worn the yellow jersey since 1919; green and polka dot mark other standings.

questions.prompt: In Greek myth, who flew too close to the sun on wings of wax and feathers?
questions.answer_note: source: Ovid's Metamorphoses — Icarus ignored his father Daedalus's warning; the sun melted his wax wings and he fell into the sea.

questions.prompt: What is the name of the symbol '&'?
questions.answer_note: source: Merriam-Webster — '&' is the ampersand, originally a ligature of the Latin word 'et' (and).

questions.prompt: How many keys are on a standard full-size piano?
questions.answer_note: source: Steinway & Sons — the modern standard piano has 88 keys: 52 white and 36 black.

questions.prompt: By law, bourbon whiskey must be made in the state of Kentucky.
questions.answer_note: source: US federal regulations (27 CFR 5) — bourbon must be made in the United States, but any state qualifies, not just Kentucky.

questions.prompt: Which artist painted The Scream?
questions.answer_note: source: National Museum of Norway — Norwegian artist Edvard Munch painted The Scream in 1893.

questions.prompt: Julius Caesar was assassinated on the Ides of which month?
questions.answer_note: source: Plutarch's Lives — Caesar was stabbed on the Ides of March, 15 March 44 BC.

questions.prompt: Which technology takes its name from a 10th-century Viking king?
questions.answer_note: source: Bluetooth SIG — the standard is named for King Harald 'Bluetooth' Gormsson; its logo combines his runic initials.

questions.prompt: Mars has exactly 2 moons. What are they called?
questions.answer_note: source: NASA — Mars's moons Phobos and Deimos were discovered by Asaph Hall in 1877; the distractors orbit Jupiter, Saturn, and Pluto.

questions.prompt: What was Disney's first full-length animated feature film, released in 1937?
options: Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs
questions.answer_note: source: Walt Disney Archives — Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs premiered in 1937; Pinocchio and Fantasia followed in 1940.

questions.prompt: In Norse mythology, what is the name of Thor's hammer?
questions.answer_note: source: the Prose Edda — Thor wields the dwarf-forged hammer Mjölnir; Gungnir is Odin's spear and Stormbreaker exists only in Marvel films.

questions.prompt: How many kilometers per second does light travel in a vacuum?
questions.answer_note: source: SI definition (BIPM) — light in a vacuum travels exactly 299,792.458 km per second, a fixed defined constant.

questions.prompt: In cricket, how many legal deliveries make up an over?
questions.answer_note: source: MCC Laws of Cricket — an over consists of 6 legal deliveries bowled from one end.

questions.prompt: Who proposed the World Wide Web at CERN in 1989?
questions.answer_note: source: CERN — British scientist Tim Berners-Lee wrote the 1989 proposal for the World Wide Web while working there.

questions.prompt: Which Spanish artist painted the 1937 anti-war mural Guernica?
questions.answer_note: source: Museo Reina Sofía, Madrid — Pablo Picasso painted Guernica in 1937; all four options are Spanish artists.

questions.prompt: Cleopatra lived closer in time to the Moon landing than to the construction of the Great Pyramid of Giza.
questions.answer_note: source: standard chronology — Great Pyramid c. 2560 BC, Cleopatra died 30 BC, Moon landing AD 1969: roughly 2,530 years versus 2,000.

questions.prompt: Which pasta's name means 'little worms' in Italian?
questions.answer_note: source: Italian etymology — vermicelli is the diminutive of 'verme' (worm); linguine means little tongues, orecchiette little ears, farfalle butterflies.

questions.prompt: Which US state shares a land border with exactly 1 other US state?
questions.answer_note: source: US Census Bureau geography — Maine borders only New Hampshire; every other bordered state touches at least 2.

questions.prompt: How many neck vertebrae does a giraffe have?
questions.answer_note: source: San Diego Zoo — giraffes have 7 cervical vertebrae, the same number as humans; each can be about 25 cm long.

questions.prompt: What is the name of Elvis Presley's Memphis mansion?
questions.answer_note: source: Graceland, Memphis — Elvis bought the mansion in 1957; it opened to the public in 1982.

questions.prompt: Which planet has the hottest surface in our solar system?
questions.answer_note: source: NASA — Venus's thick CO2 atmosphere keeps its surface near 465°C, hotter than Mercury despite being farther from the Sun.

questions.prompt: Which author created the detective Sherlock Holmes?
questions.answer_note: source: A Study in Scarlet (1887) — Arthur Conan Doyle introduced Sherlock Holmes in that novel.

questions.prompt: Nintendo was founded in the 1800s as a playing-card company.
questions.answer_note: source: Nintendo company history — founded in Kyoto in 1889 by Fusajiro Yamauchi to make hanafuda playing cards.

questions.prompt: In what year were the first modern Olympic Games held in Athens?
questions.answer_note: source: International Olympic Committee — the first modern Olympiad was held in Athens in 1896.

questions.prompt: The Wright brothers made their first powered flight in 1903 in which US state?
questions.answer_note: source: Smithsonian — the Wright Flyer flew at Kill Devil Hills near Kitty Hawk, North Carolina, on 17 December 1903; the brothers were from Ohio.

questions.prompt: Cinnamon is harvested from which part of a tree?
questions.answer_note: source: Encyclopaedia Britannica — cinnamon is the dried inner bark of Cinnamomum trees, which curls into quills as it dries.

questions.prompt: The 1942 film Casablanca is set during which war?
questions.answer_note: source: Casablanca (Warner Bros., 1942) — the film follows World War II refugees seeking exit visas in Vichy-controlled Morocco.

questions.prompt: Napoleon Bonaparte died in 1821 in exile on which island?
questions.answer_note: source: Longwood House records — Napoleon died on Saint Helena on 5 May 1821; Elba was his first exile, Corsica his birthplace.

questions.prompt: Which river flows through the 4 capital cities Vienna, Bratislava, Budapest, and Belgrade?
questions.answer_note: source: standard European geography — the Danube is the only river flowing through 4 national capitals: Vienna, Bratislava, Budapest, Belgrade.

questions.prompt: Which of these events happened first?
options: First recorded teaching at the University of Oxford
Founding of the Aztec capital Tenochtitlán
Start of construction of Notre-Dame in Paris
questions.answer_note: source: University of Oxford — teaching existed there by 1096, before Notre-Dame construction began (1163), Magna Carta (1215), and Tenochtitlán's traditional founding (1325).
